clue.text: Make challenging basket

blocks.note: first meaning: to obstruct or make something harder to do
second meaning: a large wicker basket with a lid, as for a picnic

explanation.surface: Someone is building an awkward or demanding basket, perhaps a craft project.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means hinder or impede; as a noun it is a lidded wicker basket for food.

clue.text: Only sounded religious

indicators.note: sounded means spoken out, so we want a word that is pronounced like the synonym rather than spelt like it

blocks.note: wholly, meaning entirely or solely, stands in for only

explanation.surface: A person who was devout in nothing but sound or appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: WHOLLY and HOLY are pronounced the same in most accents.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sacred or devout is connected with faith and divine worship, the core sense of religious.

clue.text: Island cocktail

blocks.note: first meaning: the island at the heart of New York City
second meaning: a drink of whiskey, sweet vermouth and bitters

explanation.definitionFit: The New York borough sits on an island, and its name is also a classic whiskey-and-vermouth mixed drink.

clue.text: Person making cryptic requires space, and fresh decor

indicators.note: fresh suggests a new version, so the letters of the following word are rearranged into a new order

blocks.note: an en is a printer's space, half an em wide
taken as written, the letters to be reshuffled

explanation.surface: Advice that a crossword setter needs room to work and a redecorated study.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a typesetting unit of space, a regular crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who turns a plain message into a cryptic, secret form is putting it into code, which is what this device or person does.

clue.text: Dock sent back tough fish

indicators.note: sent back means returned the way it came, so the synonym is written from end to start

blocks.note: to dock a tail or wages is to clip it
tough and hard are synonyms

explanation.surface: A hardy fish was turned away from the harbour dock.
explanation.walkthrough: Dock looks like a harbour, but here it is the verb meaning cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: This small oily sea creature, related to the herring and sold tinned, is a species of fish.

clue.text: Tiny map perhaps – it covers three points

indicators.note: covers means wraps around, so the first piece goes on the outside of the second

blocks.note: taken as written
north, south and east are three compass points

explanation.surface: A miniature map that takes in three locations.
explanation.walkthrough: Compass points N, S, E and W are a common crossword source of single letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A small extra picture placed inside a larger one, like a little locator chart in a corner, is this kind of panel.

clue.text: Fried item almost neutralising wine

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a chip is a fried potato stick
anti is the prefix for something that counteracts, as in antacid

explanation.surface: A fried snack nearly cancels out the effect of a glass of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a red table wine from Tuscany in Italy, traditionally sold in straw-covered flasks.

clue.text: Confuse swaying steps with splits

indicators.note: splits means leaves or departs, so the abbreviated word goes out of the longer one

blocks.note: a duck-like rocking walk
W is the standard abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A dancer's rocking steps and a gymnastic split leave the audience baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: Splits looks like the gymnastic move, but it is a verb meaning leaves; W departs from the start of WADDLE, leaving ADDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To muddle someone's thinking or befuddle their brain is to throw it into confusion.

clue.text: Who'll make setters beg, ordered to set differently

indicators.note: to set something differently is to arrange it another way, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: both words taken letter for letter as the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone who will force crossword setters to plead, told to compose puzzles another way.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters looks like crossword compilers, but here they are the gun dogs, Irish or English setters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who raises puppies of a pedigree, such as red setters, produces those animals, so this is who makes them.

clue.text: Mobile places stocking new glass protector

indicators.note: mobile means able to move about, so the letters are free to shift into a new order
stocking means holding in store, so one piece is kept inside the other

blocks.note: the six letters to be rearranged
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Phones and shops selling a fresh screen protector, as in a mobile accessory store.
explanation.walkthrough: Mobile reads as a phone, with glass protector as its screen guard; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera lens is made of glass, and the cover clipped over it shields it from scratches and dust.

clue.text: Suffer in pursuit of rubbish style

blocks.note: to pan a show is to rubbish it in a review
to ache is to suffer pain

explanation.surface: Someone endures a stylish but worthless chase.
explanation.walkthrough: In pursuit of means coming after, so the suffering piece follows the rubbish piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamboyant confidence and flair in doing something is a kind of dash or élan, that is, style.

clue.text: Do replace content in slang with established language

indicators.note: replacing the content means emptying out the middle, so only the outside letters stay
with here means filled with, so the second piece is placed inside the first

blocks.note: the first and last letters of slang
a long-established major language of India

explanation.surface: An instruction to swap the words in some slang for a formal, recognised language.
explanation.walkthrough: Do looks like a verb starting an instruction; it is the noun for a party, and the whole answer is S(HINDI)G.
explanation.definitionFit: A do is informal British for a party or celebration, and a noisy lively party is a shindig.

clue.text: He's stuffed waffle to come close to encapsulating Belgium

indicators.note: encapsulating means enclosing inside, so the country's letter goes within the preceding phrase

blocks.note: padding is verbose filler, like waffle
taken as written
to near is to approach
B is the international vehicle code for Belgium

explanation.surface: Someone has overeaten, filling up on Belgian waffles.
explanation.walkthrough: Stuffed looks like overfed, but it means filled with stuffing, as a soft toy is; B sits inside NEAR after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The marmalade-loving toy bear from Peru in the children's stories is a soft toy filled with stuffing.

clue.text: Following cat, duck plunged into drink where violence could flare

indicators.note: plunged into means dropped inside, so the duck goes within the drink

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
the cat o' nine tails was a whip, so a cat is a lash
a pint is a glass of beer
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, so zero

explanation.surface: A pub scene: after a cat chases a duck into a pond, tempers rise.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a score of zero, shown as O.
explanation.definitionFit: A tense point or situation at which conflict is likely to erupt is the moment or place where trouble could ignite.

clue.text: Some cocksure talk retracted in future

indicators.note: some means only a part, so the letters are found inside the following words
retracted means drawn back, so the found letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: letters spanning the end of cocksure and the start of talk

explanation.surface: Some overconfident boasting was taken back for the time being.
explanation.definitionFit: Afterwards, at a subsequent time, is the adverbial sense meaning in time to come.

clue.text: Throw goes with current entryway carpet

blocks.note: to cast is to throw
I is the symbol for electric current
a gate is a way in

explanation.surface: A rug that might match the current hallway decor.
explanation.walkthrough: Carpet looks like a noun for a rug; it is the verb meaning to reprimand, as in being carpeted by the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is to give them a severe telling-off, and to castigate is to criticise or rebuke harshly.

clue.text: Last ones in company now spreading free bad apps?

indicators.note: last ones means only the closing letter of each word that follows is kept
spreading means opening out to make room, so the word stretches around the other letters

blocks.note: spare and free both mean available or unoccupied
the final letters of company and now

explanation.surface: Companies are now distributing harmful free apps.
explanation.definitionFit: Malicious software secretly gathering a user's information is a type of harmful program, hence bad apps with a question mark.

clue.text: Careful visiting temporary lodging I have

blocks.note: visiting a place means being at it
a tent is a temporary shelter
the contraction I've

explanation.surface: A cautious camper staying somewhere for a short time.
explanation.definitionFit: Being watchful, considerate and paying close heed means taking care, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Polite sign-off after count

blocks.note: since means after, as in since Tuesday
to count on someone is to rely on them

explanation.surface: A courteous closing to a letter from an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: Count looks like a nobleman signing a letter; it is the verb used in count on.
explanation.definitionFit: Ending a formal letter with yours and this adverb is a conventional courteous closing formula.

clue.text: Cheese, ramen, out-of-bounds fare for vegans

indicators.note: out of bounds means the boundaries are removed, so the first and last letters go and the middle stays

blocks.note: a mild Dutch cheese
the inner letters of ramen

explanation.surface: Cheese and noodle soup are forbidden foods on a plant-based diet.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is right that cheese is off-limits for vegans, but here the cheese supplies letters, not the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Young green soybeans served in the pod are a plant food popular with those who avoid animal products.

clue.text: Swim club here ejecting old royal

indicators.note: ejecting means throwing out, so the royal's letters are removed from the word before it

blocks.note: a bat is a club used in cricket or baseball
taken as written
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.surface: A swimming club throws out an elderly member of the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen; taking it out of HERE leaves HE.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a dip or go into the sea or a pool for pleasure is to swim, in British usage.

clue.text: Monarchy curses fall

blocks.note: bah is an exclamation of annoyance, like curses!
rain is water that falls, and rain down means fall

explanation.surface: A king or queen sees their subjects swear as the regime collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: Curses reads as a verb or plural noun, but it is the mild exclamation of frustration.
explanation.definitionFit: This Gulf island state is a kingdom ruled by a king, so it is an example of a monarchy.

clue.text: After week, will he bin Pac-Man to play this?

indicators.note: after week means once the week has gone, so its abbreviation is taken away
play means move freely about, so the remaining letters are jumbled

blocks.note: all the letters of these words, taken together
W is the abbreviation for week

explanation.surface: Will a gamer give up the video game after a week to play something else?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue sets the scene of an arcade, and this refers to the game the player turns to.
explanation.definitionFit: The question asks what the player will switch to in an arcade: a coin-operated table game with flippers and a steel ball.

clue.text: Man heading off when people go out?

indicators.note: heading off means the head, or first letter, is removed

blocks.note: a chess piece is called a man, and a knight is one

explanation.surface: A man leaves at the hour when everyone goes out.
explanation.walkthrough: Man is a chess term for any piece, which yields the knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening hours after dark are when people typically go out for entertainment, hence the question mark for a cryptic hint.

clue.text: Superior pork pie brought round for one

indicators.note: brought round means turned about, so the abbreviation runs back to front

blocks.note: pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang for lie, shortened to porky
e.g. means for example, that is, for one

explanation.surface: A first-rate pork pie has been delivered for one person.
explanation.walkthrough: Pork pie is rhyming slang for lie, a British usage; it also gives the slang word porky for a fib.
explanation.definitionFit: A feudal lord to whom vassals owed allegiance was their overlord, so a crossword-friendly sense of superior.

clue.text: Spot top scorer dropping back

indicators.note: dropping the back means losing the final letter

blocks.note: Lionel Messi, the record-breaking Argentine footballer

explanation.surface: Identify the leading goal-scorer falling back into defence.
explanation.walkthrough: Spot reads as see or identify, but it is the noun for a tricky situation.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a spot is to be in trouble or a predicament, as being in a muddle or awkward fix.

clue.text: Thankless sort chosen for office grind

blocks.note: a party voted in is elected to government
to grate cheese is to grind it down

explanation.surface: An unappreciative person picked for a dull job of office drudgery.
explanation.walkthrough: Office grind reads as dull desk work; the words belong to different pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An ungrateful person fails to show gratitude, so this noun describes a thankless individual.

clue.text: Appraise retro chopper from my collection

indicators.note: retro means backward-looking, so the tool's name is written backwards

blocks.note: an axe is a chopping tool
mine means belonging to me, my own collection of things

explanation.surface: Value a vintage helicopter from a private collection.
explanation.walkthrough: Chopper suggests a helicopter or motorbike in a retro collection, but it is the woodcutter's tool.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect closely and assess the value or condition of something is to evaluate or appraise it.

clue.text: Secured Asian holiday with her newsroom boss ...

blocks.note: Tet is the Vietnamese New Year festival
taken as written
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A journalist booked a trip to Asia with her editor.
explanation.walkthrough: Tet is the lunar New Year celebration in Vietnam.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal tied by a rope to a post is fastened, so this word means fixed in place or made fast.

clue.text: ... if not one in France to a smaller extent

blocks.note: un is French for one
less means to a smaller degree

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: unless a French holiday is reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links it to the previous clue's surface but has no effect on the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjunction introduces an exception condition, meaning except on the condition that, which is the sense of if not.
